transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump says the U.S. will not resume strikes on Iran before the midterm elections.
Trump has said recently he's confident an end to the war could come in the days before or after the election,
while also saying he's open to resuming full-scale military operations.
According to a Congressional Research Service report, the war has damaged or destroyed at least 81 U.S. military aircraft and drones.
The downed aircraft include what the military has publicly acknowledged, as well as dozens it's refused to discuss.
An Army report found systemic errors led to the crash of a helicopter with a civilian plane in January 2025.
NPR's Quill Lawrence reports the collision killed 67 people just outside Washington, D.C.
The Army Black Hawk helicopter collided with an American Airlines jet in the congested air traffic over the Potomac River near Reagan National Airport.
An Army report from May that has been seen by NPR but not publicly released cites systematic failures of communication and procedure.
Amy Hunt lost four family members in the disaster.
It was systematic failures that led to this accident, and they were totally preventable.
They should have been seen by the FAA. They should have been seen by the military. They should have been seen by the air, the commercial airliners.
A bill to change procedures around this congested airspace failed in Congress last year after the Trump administration pulled its support.
The Army did not respond to a request for comment.
Quill Lawrence, NPR News.
Hurricane Isaias could make landfall on the northern Gulf Coast late tomorrow or early Saturday. NPR's Bill Chappell reports it's the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026.
It's been more than a hundred years since the Atlantic area got its first hurricane of the season this late.
But now officials are urging people to finish preparing today for Hurricane Isaias.
Forecasters believe Isaias will grow into a strong Category 2 hurricane before hitting the coast.
Parts of Mississippi, Alabama, and the Florida Panhandle are under alert for dangerous winds and a storm surge that could reach five to seven feet in some areas.
The National Hurricane Center says Isaias will move quickly after making landfall, bringing heavy rain and strong wind far inland over the weekend.
Bill Chappell, NPR News.
Margaret Hamilton, a pioneering software developer who wrote code for the Apollo moon lander, has died at the age of 90.
NPR's Jeff Brumfield has this remembrance.
Hamilton was born in Indiana and studied mathematics in college.
She became involved in the Apollo program through MIT and eventually was put in charge of the onboard flight software.
To describe the work, Hamilton coined the term software engineer. Here she is in 2017.
The engineers thought it was funny. There is Margaret again with her software engineering.
But it stuck. Hamilton received many awards throughout her career, including the Presidential Medal of Freedom from Barack Obama in 2016.
Jeff Brumfield, NPR News.
This is NPR News from Washington.
Attorneys for the family of a man shot and killed by an immigration officer in a Chicago suburb said they filed a claim for compensation.
Silverio Villegas Gonzalez was a 38-year-old Mexican national who lived in the U.S. for 18 years.
The Department of Homeland Security initially said the agent was dragged by his vehicle and seriously injured.
Police body-worn camera footage showed that the agent told officers his injuries were nothing major.
The Department of Homeland Security is proposing a rule that would charge foreign students up to $100,000 for a popular postgraduate work visa.
NPR's Alyssa Nadwareny has more.
The proposed rule would charge $70,000 for all graduates with F1 student status to participate in 12 months of optional practical training, often called OPT,
which allows recent grads a path to start a career and eventually land a job that will sponsor a longer stay.
A two-year extension available for graduates in STEM fields would cost another $30,000.
The rule aims to make it easier for American citizens to compete for jobs and is part of the administration's larger crackdown on immigration.
It is among a series of moves seeking to limit foreign students at U.S. institutions, including setting defined time limits of study.
The new proposed fees will go through a public comment period before they become final.
Alyssa Nadwareny, NPR News.
Just in time for spooky season, the old State House Museum in Little Rock is offering a paranormal investigation class this weekend.
According to the Arkansas Times, you can secure a spot in Ghost Hunting 101 for $45.
I'm Rylan Barton. This is NPR News from Washington.
Hi, it's Terry Gross.
Ladies and gentlemen, I can say that now because this administration thinks there's only two genders, and I'm both of them.
That's actor and drag king Murray Hill.
In the series Somebody Somewhere, he played the host of A Queer Cabaret, which is something he's done plenty of in real life, too.
Listen on the NPR app or wherever you listen to fresh air.
